sub_scenario.one_line: clinical trials writer: reject the assignment as currently arranged

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the protocol deviation narrative and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The clinical operations hot desks review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I assembled a deviation narrative at the medical library workstation with the source reports open side by side.
What did that allow?
I could distinguish the investigator account from the monitoring record.
Someone new shadowed me in the Friday safety review this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the library workstation into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
When I drafted the cardiac-study deviation narrative at a hot desk, Teams calls and monitor questions caused me to merge two dates.
What was the result?
The safety physician returned it because the chronology was unreliable.
I can update the enrollment tracker from the clinical operations desks.
Are those desks workable for all trial tasks?
They are fine for entering completed facts.
I archived last cycle's notes on the clinical operations hot desks and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
The library workstation is closed for inventory through Friday, and the safety review begins at 10:00.
Could you draft there beforehand?
No, it is unavailable during the only preparation window.
A vendor call about the protocol deviation narrative ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the Friday safety review checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the library workstation.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the clinical operations hot desks records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
For the oncology protocol, monitor calls at the clinical desk split my attention while I compared visit dates, and I transposed the investigator and monitoring timelines.
What did that require?
A full chronology check after the safety meeting was delayed.
I sketched next week's plan for the library workstation before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the protocol deviation narrative updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The safety physician has set Thursday evening as the last time to circulate the narrative for clinical review.
Can you wait until Friday to correct it?
No, the reviewers need the draft beforehand.
I compared two options for the clinical operations hot desks tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the Friday safety review handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
Why is the clinical operations hot-desk assignment a poor choice before Friday's safety review?
